The widened crossover short-circuits the cooling jacket.

Resistance falls sharply, but cold water entering the center bore turns through the enlarged slots near the top and exits through the outer annulus without sweeping the probe tip. This 133,181-cell rerun uses the updated widened STEP geometry.

Cooling coverage warning

The resolved bulk-flow trajectories turn outward at z ≈ 25.8 mm. The fluid volume continues to z = 2 mm, but that lower jacket is now predominantly a stagnant dead leg rather than the through-flow path.

Pressure resistance curve

Smooth interpolation through CFD points; quadratic fit Δp ≈ 0.254 Q²

What was sealed

The 0.30 mm radial clearances around the sensor, printed insert, inner tube and outer tube were treated as solid epoxy. No coolant leakage into the combustor was permitted.

What the pump must overcome

At 2 L/min the widened tip consumes only 0.011 bar before adding the remaining tubes, hoses, fittings and outlet backpressure. At 3 L/min it consumes 0.023 bar.

Change from the first geometry

The predicted loss falls by 98.7% at 2 L/min, from 81.7 to 1.06 kPa. That reduction is mostly evidence of the new short path, not proof of improved tip cooling.

Design implication

The crossover needs to remain at the hot end, or the upper route must be blocked so all coolant is forced down to the sensor before entering the outer return. Pressure drop should then be reduced by enlarging that end-turn passage locally.

Updated widened STEP; reversed flow; 133,181-cell steady k–ω SST model. A laminar cross-check at 2 L/min predicted 1.08 kPa, 2.3% above the SST result. CFD uses room-temperature incompressible water: ρ = 998 kg/m³, ν = 1.004×10⁻⁶ m²/s. Heat carried uses average cp = 4.19 kJ/kg·K and ΔT = 70 K: 4.88 kW per L/min. That is coolant enthalpy capacity, not predicted wall heat transfer. Estimated CFD uncertainty before physical validation: at least ±20%.
